wake_word._model_note: openwakeword PRETRAINED models only: alexa, hey_mycroft, hey_jarvis, hey_rhasspy, ok_nabu, timer, weather. 'hey_aadi' is NOT a pretrained model — to say 'Hey Aadi' you must train a custom model (https://github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord#training-new-models) and point custom_model_path at the resulting .onnx file.
wake_word._custom_model_path_note: Absolute path to a custom .onnx wake word model. When set, it overrides 'model'.
wake_word._allow_always_on_fallback_note: If true and no wake word model can load, Aadi skips wake word detection and goes straight to conversation mode. Set false to make a load failure loud instead of silent.

stt._model_size_note: tiny/base/small/medium/large-v3-turbo. 'small' is the practical ceiling on a 2-core CPU (~4-7 s per utterance). large-v3-turbo has better Hindi accuracy but costs 2-3x more time without a GPU.
stt._noise_guard_note: Lower min_lang_prob / raise max_no_speech_prob if real speech is being discarded. Raise min_lang_prob / lower max_no_speech_prob if background noise leaks through.
stt._allowed_languages_note: Whisper hallucinations (Korean, Turkish etc from fan noise) are discarded if detected language is not in this list. Set to null to accept all languages.
stt.initial_prompt: Speak in English or Hindi only.
stt._initial_prompt_note: Biases Whisper decoder towards English/Hindi tokens from the first frame, preventing Korean/Turkish hallucinations.
stt._low_confidence_retry_note: Bilingual safety net. When auto-detect returns a language with confidence below low_confidence_threshold, the SAME model re-runs once with language forced to retry_language, and the pass with the better average log-probability wins. Costs one extra pass only on ambiguous audio, and zero extra RAM.

llm._two_model_note: Phase 1 (intent routing) emits English-only JSON and must be fast — a 0.5B model is ideal. Phase 3 writes the actual reply and must handle Hindi Devanagari — Gemma's 262k vocab tokenises Devanagari far more efficiently than Qwen's, which matters a lot on a CPU. Ollama keeps both resident via keep_alive.

_chat_model_options.gemma3:4b: 3.3GB — best Hindi+English balance for a 2-core CPU. RECOMMENDED.
_chat_model_options.gemma4:e2b-it: ~1.2GB — fastest option with usable Hindi. Try if gemma3:4b feels slow.
_chat_model_options.gemma4:e4b-it: ~2.8GB — newer, slightly better than gemma3:4b if available.
_chat_model_options.qwen3:1.7b: 1.1GB — fast, Hindi is passable but weaker than Gemma.
_chat_model_options.qwen2.5:0.5b: 0.4GB — fallback only. Hindi output is unreliable at this size.

llm._fallback_note: If chat_model is not pulled in Ollama, fall back to router_model instead of failing. Set false to fail loudly.
llm._num_thread_note: Match physical+logical core count. This machine is 2 cores / 4 threads.

tts._kokoro_note: Kokoro covers BOTH languages in one 82M model: lang_code 'a' (American English) and 'h' (Hindi). Hindi needs espeak-ng installed for phonemes. Voice prefixes: af_/am_ = US English, bf_/bm_ = UK English, hf_/hm_ = Hindi.
tts._piper_note: Fallback engine only. Set absolute .onnx paths to enable, e.g. C:\piper\voices\en_US-amy-medium.onnx

tools._path_note: Leave null to auto-discover: PATH, the active venv's Scripts folder, your user profile, and common install locations are all searched at startup. Set an absolute path only to override.
